S.FORM: iiku ia, Muʔu.
S.PHON: iiku ia muʔu
S.FORM: iiku ia, Mu'u.
S.PHON: iiku ia muʔu
S.TRANSL: I am Mu'u.

S.FORM: tee=ku pu-a-iisua sua ni-pa-kari=cu=maku sua chiausou=maku.
S.PHON: teeku puaiisua sua nipakariʦumaku sua ʦhiausoumaku
S.FORM: teeku puaiisua sua nipakaricumaku sua chiausoumaku.
S.PHON: teeku puaiisua sua nipaka[r|ɾ]iʦumaku sua ʦhiausoumaku
S.TRANSL: I will tell the story that I've already told the professor.

S.FORM: m-ara-ʔuna=pa u-cani sua kisa-i ma-maaraŋ nakai kaʔan=pa=kamu taavalaʔə ʔinia.
S.PHON: maraʔunapa uʦani sua kisai mamaaraŋ nakai kaʔanpakamu taavaɾaʔə ʔinia
S.FORM: mara'unapa ucani sua kisai mamaarang nakai ka'anpakamu taavara'e 'inia.
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]aʔunapa uʦani sua kisai mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ nakai kaʔanpakamu taava[r|ɾ]aʔe ʔinia
S.TRANSL: There is only one story, which the elder has told before, but you don't know it yet.

S.FORM: sua tia=kari=maku makasi-in ia, sua vanai=ta miana mu-u-a-kusa-kusa ʔaupoo ia, kuinii.
S.PHON: sua tiakarimaku makaʂiin ia sua vanaita miana muuakusakusa ʔaupoo ia kuinii
S.FORM: sua tiakarimaku makasiin ia, sua vanaita miana muuakusakusa 'aupoo ia, kuinii.
S.PHON: sua tiaka[r|ɾ]imaku makaʂiin ia sua vanaita miana muuakusakusa ʔaupoo ia kuinii
S.TRANSL: What I'm going to say is the reason why we went to 'Aupoo for the Lunar New Year in the past.

S.FORM: sua ʔənai ʔaupoo ia, cu-cculu ʔənai=mita kanakanavu.
S.PHON: sua ʔənai ʔaupoo ia ʦuʦʦuɾu ʔənaimita kanakanavu
S.FORM: sua 'enai 'aupoo ia, cuccuru 'enaimita kanakanavu.
S.PHON: sua ʔenai ʔaupoo ia ʦuʦʦu[r|ɾ]u ʔenaimita kanakanavu
S.TRANSL: 'Aupoo was actually our Kanakanavu's land.

S.FORM: nain vanai-ni si ʔuuna vaatu ni-mu-ʔuna caa-caan na tia=ʔais-an.
S.PHON: nain vanaini ʂi ʔuuna vaatu nimuʔuna ʦaaʦaan na tiaʔaisan
S.FORM: nain vanaini si 'uuna vaatu nimu'una caacaan na tia'aisan.
S.PHON: nain vanaini ʂi ʔuuna vaatu nimuʔuna ʦaaʦaan na tiaʔaisan
S.TRANSL: For some reason, there was a rock on the road.

S.FORM: mia cuu-cua=kan maamia, maaraŋ pakisia, maraŋ kanakanavu, mia cuu-cua maamia.
S.PHON: mia ʦuuʦuakan maamia maaraŋ pakiʂia maraŋ kanakanavu mia ʦuuʦua maamia
S.FORM: mia cuucuakan maamia, maarang pakisia, marang kanakanavu, mia cuucua maamia.
S.PHON: mia ʦuuʦuakan maamia maa[r|ɾ]aŋ pakiʂia ma[r|ɾ]aŋ kanakanavu mia ʦuuʦua maamia
S.TRANSL: There were only two people: one was an elder Chinese, and the other was an elder Kanakanavu.

S.FORM: pu-a-iisua sua tia=pusu-aʔan, vaatu.
S.PHON: puaiisua sua tiapusuaʔan vaatu
S.FORM: puaiisua sua tiapusua'an, vaatu.
S.PHON: puaiisua sua tiapusuaʔan vaatu
S.TRANSL: (They) talked about carrying the rock on the shoulders.

S.FORM: "sua pəsə-kəna=kani pusu-aʔan, vaatu əm-əsəʔə ʔəna-ʔənai ia, tia=ŋuai tamna ʔənai," misai.
S.PHON: sua pəsəkənakani pusuaʔan vaatu əməsəʔə ʔənaʔənai ia tiaŋuai tamna ʔənai misai
S.FORM: "sua pesekenakani pusua'an, vaatu emese'e 'ena'enai ia, tianguai tamna 'enai," misai.
S.PHON: sua pesekenakani pusuaʔan vaatu emeseʔe ʔenaʔenai ia tiaŋuai tamna ʔenai misai
S.TRANSL: "The person who can lift the rock, carry it on his shoulder, and place it on the ground will own the land," they said.

S.FORM: ni-maka-pusa-n=kani pusu-aʔan sua pakisia=kan ia, mara kaʔan kaakua.
S.PHON: nimakapusankani pusuaʔan sua pakiʂiakan ia mara kaʔan kaakua
S.FORM: nimakapusankani pusua'an sua pakisiakan ia, mara ka'an kaakua.
S.PHON: nimakapusankani pusuaʔan sua pakiʂiakan ia ma[r|ɾ]a kaʔan kaakua
S.TRANSL: The Chinese tried to carry it twice on his shoulder without success, not quite sufficient strength.

S.FORM: ma-naasə kanakanavu sua ni-pusu-aʔan ʔinia.
S.PHON: manaasə kanakanavu sua nipusuaʔan ʔinia
S.FORM: manaase kanakanavu sua nipusua'an 'inia.
S.PHON: manaase kanakanavu sua nipusuaʔan ʔinia
S.TRANSL: The Kanakanavu succeeded carrying it on his shoulder.

S.FORM: si nai cəʔəra-i ʔənai ʔaupoo ia, ʔənai=cu kanakanavu.
S.PHON: ʂi nai ʦəʔərai ʔənai ʔaupoo ia ʔənaiʦu kanakanavu
S.FORM: si nai ce'erai 'enai 'aupoo ia, 'enaicu kanakanavu.
S.PHON: ʂi nai ʦeʔe[r|ɾ]ai ʔenai ʔaupoo ia ʔenaiʦu kanakanavu
S.TRANSL: Hey, let's see, all the land in 'Aupoo belongs to the Kanakanavu.

S.FORM: ma-naasə kanakanavu ni-pusu-aʔan ʔinia.
S.PHON: manaasə kanakanavu nipusuaʔan ʔinia
S.FORM: manaase kanakanavu nipusua'an 'inia.
S.PHON: manaase kanakanavu nipusuaʔan ʔinia
S.TRANSL: The Kanakanavu succeeded carrying it on his shoulder.

S.FORM: nai, cəʔəra-i, kaa-na-navuru ia, ʔənai=mita kanakanavu.
S.PHON: nai ʦəʔərai kaananavuru ia ʔənaimita kanakanavu
S.FORM: nai, ce'erai, kaananavuru ia, 'enaimita kanakanavu.
S.PHON: nai ʦeʔe[r|ɾ]ai kaananavu[r|ɾ]u ia ʔenaimita kanakanavu
S.TRANSL: Hey, let's see, we went to Navuru which is our Kanakanavu land.

S.FORM: vanai=cu maamia ʔənai pakisia kisa-ən si ma-kaasi=kani pakisia maaraŋ, "ma-manəŋ=cu, kue, nu vua-ən kimia."
S.PHON: vanaiʦu maamia ʔənai pakiʂia kisaən ʂi makaaʂikani pakiʂia maaraŋ mamanəŋʦu kue nu vuaən kimia
S.FORM: vanaicu maamia 'enai pakisia kisaen si makaasikani pakisia maarang, "mamanengcu, kue, nu vuaen kimia."
S.PHON: vanaiʦu maamia ʔenai pakiʂia kisaen ʂi makaaʂikani pakiʂia maa[r|ɾ]aŋ mamaneŋʦu kue nu vuaen kimia
S.TRANSL: The reason the land became inhabited by the Chinese is because an elderly Chinese person said, "It will be nice if (the land) is given to us!"

S.FORM: "si tiʔiŋ-ai mata ʔakia tia=tu-ʔuna-an=mia," misai=kani sua pakisia.
S.PHON: ʂi tiʔiŋai mata ʔakia tiatuʔunaanmia misaikani sua pakiʂia
S.FORM: "si ti'ingai mata 'akia tiatu'unaanmia," misaikani sua pakisia.
S.PHON: ʂi tiʔiŋai mata ʔakia tiatuʔunaanmia misaikani sua pakiʂia
S.TRANSL: "Because it is just a little (land), and there isn't enough space for us to live." the Chinese said.

S.FORM: ʔuuna=kani ma-maaraŋ ni-pu-kari ia, "nain=kusa=ʔai, maa-kai-naanu," misai=kan.
S.PHON: ʔuunakani mamaaraŋ nipukari ia nainkusaʔai maakainaanu misaikan
S.FORM: 'uunakani mamaarang nipukari ia, "nainkusa'ai, maakainaanu," misaikan.
S.PHON: ʔuunakani mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ nipuka[r|ɾ]i ia nainkusaʔai maakainaanu misaikan
S.TRANSL: The elder person said, "Who on earth was it? I don't know who it was. It does not matter."

S.FORM: iimu vanai-ni kaisiisi-in sua kaa-naa-navuru ia, kisa-ən=kiai kanakanavu si ʔənai kanakanavu.
S.PHON: iimu vanaini kaiʂiiʂiin sua kaanaanavuru ia kisaənkiai kanakanavu ʂi ʔənai kanakanavu
S.FORM: iimu vanaini kaisiisiin sua kaanaanavuru ia, kisaenkiai kanakanavu si 'enai kanakanavu.
S.PHON: iimu vanaini kaiʂiiʂiin sua kaanaanavu[r|ɾ]u ia kisaenkiai kanakanavu ʂi ʔenai kanakanavu
S.TRANSL: Therefore, the reason we go to Navuru for the (Lunar New Year) festival is that it used to be Kanakanavu land.

S.FORM: sua ʔaupoo ia, kanakanavu tamna ʔənai.
S.PHON: sua ʔaupoo ia kanakanavu tamna ʔənai
S.FORM: sua 'aupoo ia, kanakanavu tamna 'enai.
S.PHON: sua ʔaupoo ia kanakanavu tamna ʔenai
S.TRANSL: 'Aupoo is a land that belonged to Kanakanavu.

S.FORM: mu-a-ʔuna ʔinia pakisia.
S.PHON: muaʔuna ʔinia pakiʂia
S.FORM: mua'una 'inia pakisia.
S.PHON: muaʔuna ʔinia pakiʂia
S.TRANSL: The Chinese people live there (now).

S.FORM: mamisa ia, ʔakia=cu mu-a-kusa ʔinia ma-maaraŋ.
S.PHON: mamisa ia ʔakiaʦu muakusa ʔinia mamaaraŋ
S.FORM: mamisa ia, 'akiacu muakusa 'inia mamaarang.
S.PHON: mamisa ia ʔakiaʦu muakusa ʔinia mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ
S.TRANSL: Because the elders are all gone, no one is going there now.

S.FORM: c<in-m>aʔivi=cu, masi-raru ʔakia=cu ma-maaraŋ m-ari-paa-paapa ma-manəŋ taa-tiʔiŋ.
S.PHON: tʂinmaʔiviʦu maʂiraru ʔakiaʦu mamaaraŋ maripaapaapa mamanəŋ taatiʔiŋ
S.FORM: c<inm>a'ivicu, masiraru 'akiacu mamaarang maripaapaapa mamaneng taati'ing.
S.PHON: tʂinmaʔiviʦu maʂi[r|ɾ]a[r|ɾ]u ʔakiaʦu mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ ma[r|ɾ]ipaapaapa mamaneŋ taatiʔiŋ
S.TRANSL: Over the time, with the elders gone, naturally there's no one to take the younger people there anymore.

S.FORM: ʔakia=cu saihu m-ari-paa-paapa mu-kusa ʔinia.
S.PHON: ʔakiaʦu saihu maripaapaapa mukusa ʔinia
S.FORM: 'akiacu saihu maripaapaapa mukusa 'inia.
S.PHON: ʔakiaʦu saihu ma[r|ɾ]ipaapaapa mukusa ʔinia
S.TRANSL: There is no guide to take people there.

S.FORM: makasua kari=maku, nakai ʔuuna=pa u-cani pu-a-iisua.
S.PHON: makasua karimaku nakai ʔuunapa uʦani puaiisua
S.FORM: makasua karimaku, nakai 'uunapa ucani puaiisua.
S.PHON: makasua ka[r|ɾ]imaku nakai ʔuunapa uʦani puaiisua
S.TRANSL: That's my story, but there is still another story.
